decisions.reason: As an adjustable cardboard quarter-pallet display that is very close to our core offer, it likely meets aspiration levels well enough and is cheap to retain within our existing design and production routines.

The pegboard-back shelf display is still close to our established competencies, so unless its sales clearly fall below aspiration we would keep it while using organisational slack to serve niche customer needs.
This quarter-pallet cardboard display fits our standard product architecture and customer base, making it more likely to be retained as a proven variant than dropped.
The eighth-pallet format extends our existing display line with limited additional resource commitment, so boundedly rational management would keep it absent strong evidence of underperformance.

Because the wooden display pallet is somewhat farther from our paper-based core, any performance shortfall would more readily trigger problemistic search and reallocation of resources back to stronger core products.

Although technically close to our core capabilities, the media-focused quarter-pallet display serves a narrower and less robust application, so it is more likely to fall below aspiration and be discontinued.
